current_example.title: Example: Maximums and Minimums in More Complex Settings

q-181993.name: Question 1
q-181993.worked_solution:
Recall that 

- ${x}_{max}$ is the maximum of a set $S$ if ${x}_{max}\in S$ and $x\le {x}_{max}$ for all $x\in S,$ and

- ${x}_{min}$ is the minimum of a set $S$ if ${x}_{min}\in S$ and ${x}_{min}\le x$ for all $x\in S.$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}min(C) & =min{1,\,-8,\,7,\,2}=-8 \\ max(C) & =max{1,\,-8,\,7,\,2}=7\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: −8
7

q-181993.html:
Question 1
?
What are the minimum and maximum of the set C={1,−8,7,2}?
min(C)=
−8
max(C)=
7
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that

  • xmax is the maximum of a set S if xmax∈S and x≤xmax for all x∈S, and

  • xmin is the minimum of a set S if xmin∈S and xmin≤x for all x∈S.

Therefore, we have the following:

min(C)=min{1,−8,7,2}=−8max(C)=max{1,−8,7,2}=7
q-181993.knowledge_point: Finding the Maximum and Minimum of a Set

q-181731.name: Question 3
q-181731.problem:
Complete the following reasoning about the set $S=(-\infty ,1):$

The value $-99$ is not the minimum of the set $S$ because {{field-1}} and yet {{field-2}}.
q-181731.worked_solution:
Recall that ${x}_{min}$ is the minimum of a set $S$ if 

- ${x}_{min}\in S,$ and

- ${x}_{min}\le x$ for all $x\in S.$

In our case, the value $-99$ is not the minimum of the set $S$ because, for example, $-100\in S$ and yet $-100<-99.$

−98∉S

−100<−99
−100<−99
−98>−99
.

q-182007.name: Question 4
q-182007.problem:
Complete the following reasoning about the set $S=(7,\infty ):$

The value $7$ is not the minimum of the set $S$ because {{field-1}}.
q-182007.worked_solution:
Recall that ${x}_{min}$ is the minimum of a set $S$ if 

- ${x}_{min}\in S,$ and

- ${x}_{min}\le x$ for all $x\in S.$

In our case, the value $7$ is not the minimum of the set $S$ because $7\notin S.$

q-182027.name: Question 6
q-182027.problem:
What are the minimum and maximum of the set $A=(-2,1)?$

The minimum of the set {{field-1}}, and the maximum of the set {{field-2}}.
q-182027.worked_solution:
Recall that 

- ${x}_{max}$ is the maximum of a set $S$ if ${x}_{max}\in S$ and $x\le {x}_{max}$ for all $x\in S,$ and

- ${x}_{min}$ is the minimum of a set $S$ if ${x}_{min}\in S$ and ${x}_{min}\le x$ for all $x\in S.$

Notice that $-2\notin A$ and $1\notin A.$ So, we have the following:

- $min(A)=min(-2,1),$ which $\text{does not exist}$

- $max(A)=max(-2,1),$ which $\text{does not exist}$
